doc.title: Leslie Gourse interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 9, 1996

chapter: Introduction and becoming a jazz writer
title: Describing music in words for readers
summary: Rowe praises her descriptions of singers; Gourse says she bridges the gap for listeners without being a musicologist.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Playing for the audience: communicating from the bandstand

blocks.x: Well you know you that was just kind of reading my mind, in describing — when you have to describe a musical performance, I would think it’s difficult and I have to compliment you on your various ways you describe people singing — you were talking about Jon Hendricks and different singers. It’s hard to put it into words sometimes, but you made me want to go listen to the records—
—so that I could hear it again.

Yes. A girlfriend last night, Joanne Brackeen plays piano and told me she heard a singer on the radio, Kevin Mahogany, and she had never heard him before but from the way that he was singing and the way I had described him to her, she knew who it was. So that’s wonderful. I do have that ability, to tell people what it sounds like, to bridge the gap. I’m not a musicologist, and I do not try to be nor want to be. I just don’t. But I do want people to have the feeling that they know something of what’s going on musically, and why they like it and what they’re hearing, and who the people are and how it expresses them as a person, and how the music generally reflects the best of that person’s character or personality.
